english.title: Enter / attempt to enter / remain on the Tyne and Wear Metro when intoxicated

english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 4(1) and 31(1) of the Tyne and Wear Metro Byelaws made under sections 58 and 62 of the Tyneside Metropolitan Railway Act 1973.

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 30 make provisions in relation to name and addresses.
(ii) Byelaw 31(2) provides powers for the removal of persons.
(iii) Byelaw 31(3) provides that when using these powers, an authorised person, including a constable, must show his/her identification if requested.
(iv) Byelaw 31(6) provides that an authorised person acting in the course of his duties shall not be liable for breach of byelaw 4(2).
(vi) Byelaw 4(2) provides that without prejudice to Byelaws 4(2) and 4(3), where reasonable notice is, or has been, given prohibiting alcohol on any train on or of the railway, no person shall have any alcohol with him on such a train, or attempt to enter such a train, with alcohol with him.
(vii) Byelaw 4(3) provides that where an authorised person reasonably believes that any person is unfit to enter or remain on the railway or is in possession of alcohol in contravention of any provision of Byelaw 4, the authorised person may:
(a) require him to leave the railway;
(b) prevent him entering or remaining on the railway until the authorised person is satisfied that he is no longer in an unfit condition or no longer has any alcohol with him in contravention of Byelaw 4.
